rewrites.summary:
This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. Legal protections a visitor stands under are national: the 5 February 2025 national decree restricts minors' access to gender-affirming surgery and hormone treatment, trans people hired under the trans labor quota were dismissed, and the national anti-discrimination agency was abolished; the framework applies here as in every province.

Practical safety is set by the national picture: the national hate-crime observatory recorded 227 attacks based on sexual orientation or gender identity in 2025 — up 62% year on year, the highest count in its ten years of operation, roughly one every 38 hours — with perpetrators mostly security-force personnel and unknown assailants in public space, beatings the main modality, institutional violence up from 17 cases in 2024 to 64 in 2025, and 32% of incidents in police stations or prisons. Activists report police violence against trans and travesti sex workers has worsened since the current national administration took office and is worst in the more conservative interior provinces; no division-specific incident series is documented, and the division has no local reporting infrastructure to generate separate records.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: National policy turbulence: the 2025 roll-back of the gender-identity framework came by decree rather than legislation, the national anti-discrimination agency was abolished and trans labor-quota hires were dismissed; no litigation flux or comparison with neighbouring divisions specific to this division is documented in the dossier.
rewrites.localsOnly: The trans labor quota is a resident-facing employment rule; a visitor never invokes it. No resident-specific statute, enforcement series or discrimination data beyond that is recorded in the dossier.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes:
No division-specific statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is on file; the assessment rests on the country dossier's no-material-deviation finding bounded by the ±0.02 threshold, and the absence of a deviation signal is not proof of no local practice. Whether the police-violence generalization reaches this division specifically is inferential, since the sourcing names conservative interior provinces generally and the division has no local reporting infrastructure to generate separate records.

No border-screening or visitor-document practice specific to the division is recorded in the dossier, and no marriage or partner-travel finding specific to the division is documented.

rewrites.summary:

Provincially, the only incident-level signal is a police-intervention pattern: police forces of three provinces, including this division's own, intervened in the deaths of three LGBT+ people over eight days (18-26 November 2025), with this division's forces explicitly named in that documented pattern.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Litigation flux over the national framework: a national LGBT legal group announced legal action against the February 2025 decrees, and constitutional experts call them unlawful; both decrees bind every province including this one, and the roll-back is the parent-country policy signal this division sits under. No comparison with neighbouring divisions beyond the documented pattern is recorded in the dossier.
rewrites.localsOnly: No resident-specific statute, enforcement series or discrimination data specific to this division is recorded in the dossier; nothing in the sourced claims addresses birth-register practice, cultural-gender roles or resident-facing employment rules in this division.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The police-intervention pattern rests on a single national report that treats one provincial case as meaningful in a low-count country; it is a documented incident pattern, not a division-level enforcement series. rewrites.summary:
No Mendoza-specific statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is documented for transgender visitors; interior divisions without local reporting infrastructure generate few records even where risk is real, and the country-wide security picture for trans and travesti people has sharply deteriorated. A visitor therefore stands under the national framework: the February 2025 roll-back of the gender-identity framework restricts minors' access to gender-affirming surgery and hormone treatment, and an April 2025 national feature described the transgender community as facing a 'chaotic, desperate situation' amid the current national administration's policies.

Practical safety: the national hate-crime observatory recorded at least 227 attacks motivated by sexual orientation or gender identity in 2025 — up 62% year on year, the highest figure of its decade of operation, roughly one every 38 hours — with perpetrators predominantly security-force personnel and unidentified attackers in public space, beatings the main modality. Attacks continued into early 2026, including a life-endangering home invasion of the president of an LGBTIQ+ organisation in a northern province.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: National policy turbulence: the national hate-crime observatory attributes the 2025 surge to the national government's 'cultural battle' and its accompanying treatment of LGBTI+ people; the national anti-discrimination agency was abolished in 2024 and trans labor-quota hires were dismissed under the current national administration; no litigation flux or comparison with neighbouring divisions specific to this division is documented in the dossier.
rewrites.localsOnly: The trans labor quota is a resident-facing employment rule; a visitor never invokes it. No resident-specific statute, enforcement series or discrimination data beyond that is recorded in the dossier.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The Washington Blade feature page cited for the 'chaotic, desperate situation' description is no longer retrievable, so those claims cannot be re-verified from the source itself. The home-invasion attack is a single documented event in a northern province rather than a division-level series or incident in this division. No border-screening or visitor-document practice specific to the division is recorded in the dossier, and no marriage or partner-travel finding specific to the division is documented.
